questions.text: If the owner, manager or chairperson is away for two weeks, another named person can run buying, selling and payments using written instructions.
anchors: Nothing works when the main person is away
Someone helps informally, but cannot access money or contracts
A named deputy exists, but has no written instructions or access
A named deputy has written instructions and can approve routine payments
Deputy tested during an absence in the last 12 months, with written instructions and signing rights

evidence.requirement: Ask who deputised last time and look for written instructions and signing rights.

questions.text: Our owner, manager or leaders completed training in business, farm or group management in the last 2 years, and we can show it.
anchors: No training in the last 2 years
Attended one short event, with no certificate or notes
Attended training and can describe what was learned
Attended training and used at least one new practice, shown in records
Attended training and use several new practices, with a plan for further training of leaders

evidence.requirement: Ask for certificates, attendance lists or training notes and one example of change made.

questions.text: We have a written plan for who leads or owns the enterprise or group if the current leader leaves, falls ill or dies.
anchors: No plan, and nobody has discussed it
Plan discussed but not written down
Written plan naming successors or a process, known to the board, family or members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the written plan and who knows about it.

questions.text: Our members elect leaders at a general meeting, and each member has one vote.
anchors: Leaders were never elected, or are appointed by one person
Leaders were elected more than 4 years ago and not since
Leaders elected in the last 4 years, but voting was by show of a few people
Leaders elected at a general meeting with most members voting, one member one vote
Elections held on schedule in by-laws, with voter list, minutes and results shown to members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the election minutes, attendance list and by-laws.

questions.text: Most members attend our general meetings, and each year they receive a report on money, sales and decisions.
anchors: No general meeting held in the last 2 years
General meeting held but under a third of members attended, no report given
A meeting held in the last year, with a verbal report only
Meeting held in the last year with over half of members and a written or read-out annual report
Yearly meeting with over two thirds of members and a written report on accounts, sales and decisions, with questions recorded

evidence.requirement: Ask for the meeting minutes, attendance list and last annual report.

questions.text: Most members sell most of their crop through the group, and we know how much they sold elsewhere.
anchors: Members sell under 10 percent of their crop through the group, or we do not know
Members sell 10 to 24 percent through the group
Members sell 25 to 49 percent through the group
Members sell 50 to 74 percent through the group, measured for at least half of members
Members sell 75 percent or more through the group, measured from member records

evidence.requirement: Compare group purchase records with member production estimates for last season.

questions.text: The roles of owner or board, managers and staff or members, and who can approve spending and sign contracts, are written down and followed.
anchors: Roles and approval powers are not written
Roles are known verbally, with no approval limits
Roles are written, but approval powers are unclear
Roles and approval limits are written and mostly followed
Roles, approval limits and signing powers are written, signed, followed and reviewed yearly

evidence.requirement: Ask for job descriptions, by-laws or an approval policy and check one recent contract or payment.

questions.text: No child below 15 works in our enterprise or on our farm, and no one under 18 does hazardous work such as spraying chemicals or carrying heavy loads.
anchors: Children below 15 work regularly on our farm or enterprise, or do hazardous work
Children help during school time or do hazardous tasks sometimes
Children help only outside school hours on light tasks, with no policy
We have a rule against child labour and children do not do hazardous tasks, but we do not check
Written rule, ages checked for all workers and suppliers, school attendance protected, and issues recorded and fixed

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the rule, worker ages and what is done when a child is found working.

questions.text: In the last 12 months our staff, members or workers received training in a skill we need, such as good farming practice, storage or record keeping, with an attendance list.
anchors: No training in the last 12 months
Informal advice only
One training session with an attendance list
Two or more sessions covering different skills, with attendance lists
A yearly training plan based on gaps, delivered, attendance recorded and results checked

evidence.requirement: Ask for the training plan, attendance lists and examples of skills used afterwards.

questions.text: An extension officer, agronomist or technical adviser visited our farms or members at least once in the last season, and we recorded the advice.
anchors: Never visited
Rarely visited, advice not recorded
Visited once, advice recorded
Visited at least twice with advice recorded
Visited regularly (about monthly in the season) with advice recorded and applied

evidence.requirement: Look for visit notes, officer names and what changed after visits.

questions.text: Members or outgrowers who take group inputs or credit repay on time, and we keep a record of who owes what.
anchors: Under 50 percent of credit was repaid on time, or no record is kept
50 to 69 percent repaid on time, records incomplete
70 to 84 percent repaid on time, records complete
85 to 94 percent repaid on time, records complete
95 percent or more repaid on time, from a complete signed ledger

evidence.requirement: Compare the ledger of credit given with repayments received last season.

questions.text: We pay the farmers, members or suppliers who sell to us on the date we promised, and they receive a payment slip or message.
anchors: Under 50 percent of payments are on the promised date
50 to 69 percent on the promised date
70 to 84 percent on the promised date
85 to 94 percent on the promised date
95 percent or more on the promised date, with slips or messages kept

evidence.requirement: Compare promised dates, payment dates and slips for three suppliers.

questions.text: Members, outgrowers, workers and suppliers have a known way to raise a complaint, and we record and answer complaints.
anchors: No way to complain
Complaints are heard informally, with no record
A person is named for complaints, but nothing is recorded
Complaints are recorded and most are answered within a month
Known channel (box, phone, committee), all complaints recorded, answered and reported to leaders or members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the complaints log and one case history.

questions.text: We keep a register of the farms or plots we farm or buy from, showing the owner, crop, area in acres and where the plot is.
anchors: No register of farms or plots
A list of names only
Register with names and crops, no areas or location
Register with names, crops, area and village or landmark for most plots
Register with names, crops, measured area and GPS point or sketch map for nearly all plots, updated each season

evidence.requirement: Ask for the register and check three plots against it.

questions.text: We keep batch and stock records that show what came in, what went out and what is in the store, updated each time stock moves.
anchors: No stock records
Stock counted occasionally, nothing written
Stock book written, but updated only weekly or monthly
Stock book updated at each movement, with batch numbers on most lots
Stock cards by batch updated at each movement, counted monthly and matched to the book

evidence.requirement: Do a physical count of one product and compare with the stock record.

questions.text: We give a receipt or delivery note for every sale or purchase, and keep a copy.
anchors: Never
Rarely, only if asked
Sometimes, for large transactions
Usually, for most transactions with copies kept
Always, numbered, with copies filed and matched to the cash book

evidence.requirement: Check three recent transactions for numbered receipts or notes with copies.

questions.text: We keep important records (contracts, receipts, member lists, accounts) for at least 2 years in a safe place, with a copy kept elsewhere.
anchors: Records are lost, scattered or kept for less than a year
Records are kept loosely at home or in the store
Records are filed in one place, with no copy
Records are filed in one safe place and key items are copied or photographed
Records are filed, copied or backed up off site, and we can find any item from the last 2 years in a day

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the file store and retrieve a record from last season.

questions.text: We use mobile money or bank transfers to pay farmers and workers, and to receive payment from buyers, for most of our transactions.
anchors: Almost all transactions are in cash (under 10 percent digital)
10 to 29 percent of transactions are digital
30 to 59 percent of transactions are digital
60 to 89 percent of transactions are digital
90 percent or more of transactions are digital, with statements kept

evidence.requirement: Compare cash and digital payments over a month of records.

questions.text: We keep our records on a phone app, spreadsheet or computer system, with backups, and not only on paper.
anchors: No digital records
Photos of paper records only
One spreadsheet or app used for one record type
Spreadsheet or app used for sales, stock and costs, backed up occasionally
Spreadsheet or app used for all core records, backed up weekly, with named person responsible

evidence.requirement: Ask to see the app or spreadsheet and the last backup.

questions.text: Each month we compare our mobile money or bank statement with our own records and explain any difference.
anchors: Never
Rarely, only when something is missing
Sometimes, but we do not explain differences
Usually monthly, with differences noted
Every month, differences explained and signed by a second person

evidence.requirement: Look for a reconciliation sheet for the last three months.

questions.text: Passwords, PINs and signing rights for our accounts and wallets are held only by authorised people and are not shared informally.
anchors: PINs and passwords are shared widely or written openly
Several informal users share one wallet or login
Authorised users are known, but one login is shared
Each authorised person has own login and PIN, with some informal sharing seen
Each authorised person has own login and PIN, access is reviewed when roles change, and no sharing is observed

evidence.requirement: Ask who can access each account and check the signatory list.

questions.text: Leaders or owners review sales, costs, stock and loan balances at least monthly in a meeting or written note.
anchors: Never
Once or twice a year
Quarterly
Monthly, but without written notes
Monthly with written notes and actions followed up

evidence.requirement: Look for the last three review notes or minutes.

questions.text: We track at least five measures with targets, such as yield per acre, cost per bag, deliveries on time, repayment rate and post-harvest loss.
anchors: We track none
We track one or two measures with no targets
We track three or four measures, targets for some
We track five or more measures with targets, reviewed each season
We track five or more measures with targets and trends over 3 seasons, shown to leaders or members

evidence.requirement: Ask for the scorecard or dashboard and the last season values.

questions.text: We collect data from our members, outgrowers or suppliers each season (area, expected and actual output, inputs received) and use it to plan.
anchors: No data collected
Data from a few leaders only
Data from half of members or suppliers, not used for planning
Data from most members or suppliers and used for planning volumes
Data from nearly all members or suppliers, checked on a sample, and used to plan purchases, inputs and finance

evidence.requirement: Ask for the last season data sheets and the plan that used them.

questions.text: Last season's results changed something we did this season, and we can name the change and the result that led to it.
anchors: Nothing changed, and results were not discussed
We talked about results, but changed nothing
We changed one thing without linking to records
We changed one thing and can link it to a recorded result
We changed several things, linked to records, and we tracked whether the change worked

evidence.requirement: Ask for an example and the record that led to the change.

questions.text: Our business, farm group or cooperative is legally registered with the right body (Registrar General or Department of Cooperatives) and the registration is current.
anchors: Not registered
Registration started but not completed
Registered, but certificate or annual returns are out of date
Registered, certificate current, annual returns filed in the last year
Registered, certificate current, returns filed, and by-laws or regulations on file and followed

evidence.requirement: Ask for the registration certificate and the latest annual return or audit letter.

questions.text: We have a Tax Identification Number and we filed the tax returns that apply to us on time in the last year.
anchors: No TIN and no returns filed
TIN held, but no returns filed in the last year
Returns filed late or incomplete
Returns filed on time for the last year
Returns filed on time for the last 2 years with proof of filing and any payments
questions.riskTag: Tax filings not up to date

evidence.requirement: Ask for the TIN certificate and filing acknowledgements.

questions.text: We hold written proof of our right to use the land we farm or store on (lease, allocation letter, customary grant record or title), covering at least the next 3 years.
anchors: No proof of right to use the land
Verbal permission only
Written note from the owner without witnesses or dates
Written agreement with the owner or traditional authority covering the next 3 years
Registered or witnessed document covering at least the crop cycle or tree life, held by the enterprise

evidence.requirement: Ask for the land documents and check the signatories and dates.

questions.text: We know whether our farming or processing activity qualifies for a tax incentive, and we have claimed what applies to us.
anchors: We do not know of any tax incentive
We have heard of incentives but have not checked if we qualify
We checked and qualify, but have not claimed
We checked and claimed one incentive that applies
We checked all that apply, claimed them, and hold proof from the tax authority or our tax adviser

evidence.requirement: Ask for the tax advice, claim or approval letter.

questions.text: We hold the current registrations, licences and permits that our activity needs from the agencies that regulate us (for example FDA, EPA, PPRSD, TCDA or Department of Cooperatives).
anchors: We hold none and do not know which apply
We know some apply but hold none
We hold some, and know of gaps
We hold all we need, current
We hold all we need, current, with a renewal calendar kept and followed

evidence.requirement: Ask for a list of applicable regulators and each certificate or licence with expiry dates.

questions.text: We hold a TCDA export permit and proof of payment of the development levy before each export shipment of raw shea or cashew.
anchors: We export raw shea or cashew without a permit
We have applied for a permit but have not received it
We hold a permit but have no levy proof for shipments
We hold a permit and levy proof for most shipments
We hold a current permit and levy proof for every shipment, filed with phytosanitary papers
questions.applies: Exports raw shea or cashew only

evidence.requirement: Ask for the TCDA permit, levy receipts and the file for the last shipment.

questions.text: Our store or processing site and the food products we sell meet FDA requirements for what we do (licence, premises, labelling and records).
anchors: No FDA licence or inspection, and we do not know the requirements
We know the requirements but meet few of them
We meet some requirements, with open gaps from an inspection or checklist
We meet most requirements and hold a valid licence
We meet all requirements, hold a valid licence, and have no open inspection findings

evidence.requirement: Review the FDA licence and the last inspection report, and visit the premises.

questions.text: We are certified, or following a written plan with dates to be certified, for the standard our target markets require (for example organic, Fairtrade, GlobalG.A.P. or the Global Shea Alliance programme).
anchors: No certification and no knowledge of what markets require
We know the standard but have no plan
We have started preparation, with no dates
We have a written plan with dates and a budget, and have done a gap check
We hold a current certificate or approved status, and passed the last audit
questions.riskTag: Not certified or planning to be

evidence.requirement: Ask for the certificate, audit report or the written plan and gap check.

questions.text: At least once a year we check our own practices against the standard or buyer rules we follow, and fix what we find.
anchors: Never, we do not check
Only when a buyer or auditor visits
Once in the last 2 years
Yearly, with findings listed
Yearly, with findings listed, fixed by a date and checked

evidence.requirement: Look for the self-assessment checklist and the corrective actions.

questions.text: We use only registered pesticides, applied by trained people wearing protective gear, and we record what was applied, where and when.
anchors: Unregistered or banned chemicals are used, or no protection and no records
Registered chemicals mostly, but no protective gear or records
Registered chemicals and some protective gear, no records
Registered chemicals, trained sprayers with protective gear, records kept for most applications
Registered chemicals only, trained sprayers, protective gear, empty containers handled safely, and complete records

evidence.requirement: Inspect the chemical store, sprayer equipment and the application record.

questions.text: We have a written list of the main risks to our enterprise (weather, price, theft, buyer default, illness) with at least one action for each.
anchors: No list of risks
Risks discussed verbally
Written list of risks without actions
Written list with an action for most risks
Written list with actions, owners and dates, reviewed each season

evidence.requirement: Ask for the risk list and a recent update.

questions.text: We have insurance on at least one major risk to our crop, livestock, stock or equipment, and we know what the policy covers.
anchors: No insurance and no knowledge of options
We know of options but have none
Insurance on one asset, but we cannot say what it covers
Insurance on our main crop, livestock or stock, with cover known
Insurance on our main risks, with premium budgeted, policy on file, and a claim process known

evidence.requirement: Ask for the policy, premium receipt and cover summary.

questions.text: Before we sell on credit or give inputs on credit to a new customer or member, we check their record and set a credit limit in writing.
anchors: We give credit to anyone who asks
We give credit to people we know, with no limits
We set limits for some customers, not written
We check record and set written limits for most customers
We check record, set written limits, and review overdue accounts monthly

evidence.requirement: Ask for the credit policy and the aged debtors list.

questions.text: We have a written plan with at least two actions for a dry spell, flood or pest outbreak, such as early maturing seed, staggered planting or a second income.
anchors: No plan for any weather or pest shock
We talk about shocks but have no plan
Plan for one shock only, with one action
Plan covering two or three shocks with at least two actions each
Written plan with actions, owners and costs, tested or used in the last 3 seasons

examples: Seed purchase for early maturing varieties
evidence.requirement: Ask for the plan and an example of when it was last used.

questions.text: Each season we obtain the seasonal rainfall forecast or weather advisory (for example from the Ghana Meteorological Agency or a radio or phone service) and use it to time planting and other work.
anchors: Never use any forecast
Rarely, only if we hear it by chance
Sometimes, but we do not change our plans
Usually receive it and have changed timing at least once
Always receive it before planting, record how it changed our timing, and share it with members or staff

evidence.requirement: Ask for the forecast received and an example of changed planting or spraying dates.

questions.text: Last season we spread risk by planting on staggered dates, or by planting drought or heat tolerant varieties on part of our area.
anchors: No staggering and no tolerant varieties
Under 10 percent of area used one of these methods
10 to 24 percent of area used one of these methods
25 to 49 percent of area used one of these methods
50 percent or more of area used one or both of these methods, shown in the season plan

evidence.requirement: Check the planting dates by plot and seed receipts or variety names.

questions.text: We keep a record of weather and pest shocks (dry spells, floods, outbreaks) and their cost to us in each of the last 3 seasons.
anchors: No record of any shocks
Verbal memory of shocks, with no figures
Written notes for the last season, with no cost
Written record with cost for the last season
Written record with dates and cost for the last 3 seasons

evidence.requirement: Ask for the record and compare with yield or loss records.

questions.text: We have a plan to look after our land, trees and water, for example tree planting, soil care and no bush burning, and we followed it last season.
anchors: No plan, and bush burning or tree cutting without replanting is common
Informal intention only
Written plan covering one area (trees, soil or water)
Written plan covering trees, soil and water, followed in part
Written plan with targets, followed and counted (trees planted, plots under soil care, fire breaks)
questions.riskTag: No land and water care plan

evidence.requirement: Ask for the plan, then visit a plot or tree site to check.

questions.text: On most of our area we use practices that keep soil fertile, such as legume rotation, manure or compost, crop residue cover or contour ridges.
anchors: No soil care practice on any area
Practices on under 10 percent of area
Practices on 10 to 29 percent of area
Practices on 30 to 59 percent of area
Practices on 60 percent or more of area, recorded in the season plan or field notes

evidence.requirement: Check field notes and visit two plots to see the practice.

questions.text: Our farm, processing site or store holds the EPA registration or permit that its size and activity require, or EPA has confirmed in writing that none is needed.
anchors: We do not know whether we need an EPA registration or permit
We know it may apply but have not applied
We applied and are waiting, with receipts
We hold the registration or permit required
We hold the permit, meet its conditions, and keep the compliance records

evidence.requirement: Ask for the permit or EPA letter and compare the size of operation with EPA thresholds.

questions.text: We dispose of waste from our farm or site (empty chemical containers, processing waste, plastic) safely, away from water sources and food.
anchors: Waste is dumped or burned near water, food or homes
Waste is left in the open and empty chemical containers are reused
Waste is gathered in one place but not safely disposed
Waste is separated, and empty chemical containers are punctured and stored away from food
Waste is separated, safely disposed or reused, with a written routine and a named person

evidence.requirement: Visit the waste area and ask how containers and processing waste are handled.

questions.text: Women who farm with us, supply us or work for us take part in decisions and have a say in how money from sales is used.
anchors: Women are not asked, and men decide how sales money is used
Women are asked occasionally, but men decide
Women speak in meetings, but do not influence how sales money is used
Women take part in decisions and influence some spending of sales money
Women take part in decisions and share control over use of sales money, shown in minutes or reports

evidence.requirement: Ask women members or staff directly, and review minutes or payment records.

questions.text: Women who farm with us can own or use the land, trees, tools and equipment they need through our group or enterprise, in their own name or jointly.
anchors: Women have no access to land, trees or equipment through us
Women can use assets only through male relatives
Women can use some assets, with no written rights
Women have written use rights to some assets
Women have written rights in own name or jointly to land, trees or equipment, with examples checked

evidence.requirement: Ask women members to describe their access and check lease, share or allocation records.

questions.text: Women hold leadership roles or sit on committees, and at least one third of leaders or managers are women.
anchors: No women in any leadership role
Women hold under 10 percent of leadership roles
Women hold 10 to 24 percent of leadership roles
Women hold 25 to 33 percent of leadership roles
Women hold more than one third of leadership roles, including at least one office-bearer post

evidence.requirement: Count leaders and committee members from the current list.

questions.text: Young people (aged 18 to 35) have defined roles or paid work with us, such as in production, aggregation, processing or records, and we know how many.
anchors: No young people involved
A few young people help informally, unpaid
Young people have some paid work, but we have no count
We can count the young people in paid or defined roles
We count young people by role, they take part in decisions or training, and we track their numbers each season

examples: Staff or member list with ages
evidence.requirement: Ask for the list of young workers or members and their roles.

questions.text: We can state in one sentence which entrepreneurs we serve, what problem we help them solve and what should change for them.
anchors: No agreed statement; leaders give different answers when asked separately
Target is described broadly (for example 'all SMEs') with no problem or change named
A statement exists but misses one of: who, which problem, what changes
Written statement covers who, problem and change, and two leaders give consistent answers
Board approved statement names stage, sector and area and is reflected in selection criteria and reports

evidence.requirement: Written mission or programme statement, plus separate interviews with two leaders compared with the selection criteria.

questions.text: We have a written theory of change that links our activities to the results we expect for entrepreneurs.
anchors: No written theory of change or results framework
Activities are listed in proposals but no link to expected results is shown
A theory of change exists but its links have no stated assumptions
Written theory of change shows activities, outputs, outcomes and key assumptions
Written theory of change shows activities, outputs, outcomes and key assumptions, has an indicator for each outcome and keeps a dated version history

examples: Theory of change diagram or narrative
evidence.requirement: The current theory of change or results framework and its version history.

questions.text: We have tested at least one assumption in our theory of change against our own data and changed the programme as a result.
anchors: The theory of change has not been reviewed since it was written
Reviewed informally in staff meetings with no record of changes
Reviewed once, findings noted but no programme change followed
Reviewed at least yearly using our own data, with at least one programme change recorded
Reviewed at least yearly using our own outcome data and entrepreneur views, with a programme change recorded and re-checked the following year

evidence.requirement: Review notes on the theory of change linked to a documented programme change.

questions.text: Most enterprises we supported in the last twelve months fit the target segment in our written mission or strategy.
anchors: Under 40 percent fit, or no written segment to check against
40 to 59 percent fit
60 to 74 percent fit
75 to 89 percent fit
90 percent or more fit, checked against the client database
questions.riskTag: Mission drift away from target segment

examples: Client database extract for last 12 months
evidence.requirement: Written target segment definition and a client database extract with stage, sector and location. The verifier counts the share that fits.

questions.text: Our curriculum and support are adapted to the sectors, languages and business conditions of the enterprises we serve, not imported unchanged.
anchors: Materials are imported from other programmes with no local change
Some local examples added with no input from local entrepreneurs or practitioners
Some modules adapted using staff knowledge only
Curriculum adapted with documented input from local entrepreneurs, mentors or sector practitioners
Curriculum adapted with documented local input, with local cases, language and sector data in the modules and a revision after each cohort

examples: Notes of consultation with entrepreneurs or sector experts
evidence.requirement: Curriculum files compared with the original source materials, and records of local input.

questions.text: We chose our programme length, cohort size and support intensity deliberately for the enterprises we serve, and can explain why.
anchors: Format copied from a funder or another programme with no rationale
Format set by budget or convenience; rationale given only verbally
A written rationale exists but is not linked to enterprise needs or evidence
Written rationale links length, cohort size and intensity to enterprise needs and stage
Written rationale links length, cohort size and intensity to enterprise needs and stage, draws on our own results or outside evidence, and the format was adjusted after a review

evidence.requirement: Programme design note explaining length, cohort size and intensity, and any later adjustment.

questions.text: Our programme design includes scheduled peer learning among entrepreneurs in the same cohort.
anchors: No peer learning; entrepreneurs meet only staff or mentors one to one
Entrepreneurs meet at events but no peer sessions are planned
Peer sessions are held occasionally, without structure or records
Peer sessions are scheduled in every cohort with a facilitation guide and attendance records
Peer sessions run in every cohort with a facilitation guide and attendance records, and entrepreneur feedback on them is collected and used to adjust later sessions

evidence.requirement: Programme schedule showing peer sessions, with attendance records and feedback.

questions.text: We design new programmes around what target entrepreneurs tell us they need, not only around what funders offer to pay for.
anchors: Programmes are designed only to match funder calls
Entrepreneurs are consulted informally after the design is fixed
Needs were gathered for some programmes but not written up
A written needs assessment from target entrepreneurs informed each programme designed in the last two years
A written needs assessment from target entrepreneurs informed each programme designed in the last two years, and a funded activity was reshaped or declined because it did not fit their needs

evidence.requirement: Needs assessments or survey results dated before programme design, and an example of a design change driven by them.

questions.text: We know which other organisations serve the same enterprises in our area and how our offer differs from theirs.
anchors: We do not know what other providers do
Leaders can name a few providers but have not compared offers
A list of providers exists but is out of date or lacks offer details
Current list of providers with services and target groups, reviewed in the last 12 months
Current list of providers with services and target groups, reviewed in the last 12 months, and our positioning and referral choices use the gaps and overlaps it shows

evidence.requirement: Provider mapping or ecosystem map with a review date, and examples of referrals or positioning decisions based on it.

questions.text: We have an estimate of how many enterprises fit our target segment in our area and the share of them we reach each year.
anchors: No estimate of the target population
Rough figure quoted from memory with no source
Estimate taken from a published or partner source but no reach share worked out
Estimate with a named source and reach share calculated in the last 12 months
Estimate with a named source and reach share calculated in the last 12 months, with reach share tracked yearly by area or sector and used to set targets

evidence.requirement: A document showing the population estimate, its source and the reach calculation.

questions.text: We have a written strategic plan with measurable targets that leaders review at least once a year.
anchors: No written plan
The plan is a funding proposal or concept note only
A written plan exists but has no measurable targets or is over three years old
A plan under three years old has measurable targets and was reviewed in the last 12 months
A board approved plan under three years old has measurable targets, a budget linked to them, a review in the last 12 months and an annual progress report

evidence.requirement: Current strategic plan and the latest annual review.

questions.text: Our programme delivery model is written down well enough that a trained new team or a new location could run it.
anchors: The model exists only in the heads of founders or key staff
Slide decks or proposals describe the model but give no operating steps
Some processes are documented with major gaps in selection, delivery or follow up
A written manual covers selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data collection
A written manual covers selection, delivery, mentoring, follow up and data collection, and two teams or sites have used it with documented adjustments
questions.riskTag: Delivery model not documented for scale

examples: Notes from a second team or site using it
evidence.requirement: Operating manual or standard procedures, and evidence of use by someone other than its authors.

questions.text: Before adding cohorts, locations or programmes, we check that we have enough staff, mentors and funding to keep quality.
anchors: Expansion is decided when funding is offered, without a capacity check
Leaders discuss capacity informally
Capacity is checked for finance only
A written capacity check covers staff, mentors, funding and quality for each expansion decision
A written capacity check covers staff, mentors, funding and quality for each expansion decision, quality indicators are tracked afterwards and growth is paused if they fall

evidence.requirement: Expansion decision notes showing a capacity check, and quality data after the last expansion.

questions.text: We select enterprises using written criteria that at least two reviewers score independently.
anchors: Selection is by one person or personal contact, with no written criteria
Criteria are understood informally and one person decides
Written criteria exist but are not shared with applicants or not scored consistently
Published criteria are scored by two or more reviewers on a scoring sheet
Published criteria are scored by two or more reviewers on a scoring sheet, score differences are discussed, decisions are minuted and criteria are reviewed after each round

evidence.requirement: Selection criteria, completed scoring sheets from at least two reviewers, and selection minutes for the last round.

questions.text: We keep a record of every applicant at every stage, with the reason for each selection or rejection.
anchors: No application records are kept beyond selected enterprises
Applications sit in email or paper files and are not collated
A list of applicants and outcomes exists without reasons
A database lists all applicants, the stage reached and the reason for each decision
A database lists all applicants, the stage reached and the reason for each decision, and the data is analysed, for example by comparing selected with rejected applicants

examples: Analysis of selected versus rejected applicants
evidence.requirement: Applicant database or register for the last round, including rejected applicants.

questions.text: We can show that we reach entrepreneurs who would not otherwise be supported, not only those already funded or well connected.
anchors: Most participants were already funded or supported elsewhere, or this is not recorded
Participants come mainly from leaders' own networks
Some outreach beyond networks, but no data on prior support
Application form records prior support, and at least half of participants had received none
Application form records prior support and at least half of participants had none, results are compared for those with and without prior support, and outreach is adjusted

examples: Application form with prior support question
Share of participants with no prior support
evidence.requirement: Application data on prior support and the outreach plan.

questions.text: Each selected enterprise receives a baseline diagnostic that leads to a written support plan within 30 days of starting.
anchors: Under 20 percent of the last cohort, or no baseline diagnostic is used
20 to 49 percent
50 to 74 percent
75 to 94 percent
95 percent or more, with support plans on file
questions.riskTag: No baseline diagnostic or support plan

evidence.requirement: Diagnostic forms and support plans for the last cohort with dates. The verifier counts those done within 30 days.

questions.text: Most of our support time goes to the needs entrepreneurs rank highest, such as sales, finance access or hiring, not mainly to pitch preparation.
anchors: Support is mostly pitch decks and general workshops; needs are never asked
Needs are asked at entry but support follows a fixed curriculum
Some modules adapt to stated needs, and time use is not tracked
Session or time records show most hours go to the top three needs the entrepreneurs ranked
Session or time records show most hours go to the top three needs the entrepreneurs ranked, needs are re-ranked mid programme and support is re-planned where they changed
questions.riskTag: Support not matched to entrepreneur needs

evidence.requirement: Needs ranking from entrepreneurs and a session or time log showing where support hours went.

questions.text: Entrepreneur feedback on mentors and sessions leads to documented changes in how we deliver.
anchors: No feedback is collected
Informal comments are heard but nothing is recorded
Feedback forms are collected but not analysed
Feedback is analysed each cohort and at least one documented change was made
Feedback is analysed each cohort and at least one documented change was made, changes are reported back to entrepreneurs and ratings are tracked across cohorts

examples: Change log or minutes citing feedback
evidence.requirement: Feedback forms or survey results and the change record that followed.

questions.text: Each entrepreneur is matched to a mentor or coach using a written view of the entrepreneur's needs and the mentor's expertise.
anchors: Mentors are assigned by availability or personal contact, with no assessment
Staff match by judgement and give no written reasons
Matches are recorded but based only on sector, not on need
Match records show the need and the mentor's expertise, and the entrepreneur may ask for a change
Match records show the need and the mentor's expertise, the entrepreneur may ask for a change, match quality is tracked and mismatches are corrected within 30 days

evidence.requirement: Match records for the last cohort and mentor profiles.

questions.text: Market access support, such as buyer introductions or market information, is a deliberate part of our offer with named activities.
anchors: No market access support is offered
Occasional introductions happen when staff happen to know a buyer
Market access sessions are included with no buyer or channel partner involved
Planned market access activities name buyers or channels and record who took part
Planned market access activities name buyers or channels and record who took part, and sales or contracts that result are tracked for participating enterprises
questions.riskTag: Market access not part of the offer

examples: Contracts or orders recorded after linkage
evidence.requirement: Programme plan showing market access activities, buyer participation records and any sales tracking.

questions.text: We have written criteria and a process for graduating, pausing or exiting enterprises from our programmes.
anchors: No graduation or exit rules; enterprises drift
Practice is informal and decided case by case
Criteria are written for graduation only
Written criteria and process for graduation, pausing and exit are applied to every enterprise
Written criteria and process for graduation, pausing and exit are applied to every enterprise, decisions are recorded and exited enterprises get a closing review and referral

evidence.requirement: Graduation and exit policy plus decision records for the last cohort.

questions.text: We were in contact with most alumni of our last three cohorts during the past twelve months.
anchors: Under 20 percent contacted, or there is no alumni list
20 to 39 percent contacted
40 to 59 percent contacted
60 to 79 percent contacted
80 percent or more contacted, with contact dates recorded

examples: Alumni database with last contact date
evidence.requirement: Alumni list with dated contact records. The verifier calculates the share contacted in the last 12 months.

questions.text: After the programme ends, alumni have a defined follow-up offer, such as clinics, mentor access or investor sessions, with clear eligibility.
anchors: No support is offered after the programme ends
Alumni can call staff for informal help
Follow-up events are held occasionally for all alumni
A written follow-up offer states eligibility, schedule and the responsible staff member
A written follow-up offer states eligibility, schedule and the responsible staff member, is adjusted by alumni stage, and its uptake and outcomes are recorded

evidence.requirement: The written alumni offer and records of alumni who used it.

questions.text: Alumni contribute back to our programmes, for example as mentors, speakers or referrers of new applicants.
anchors: No alumni involvement
Alumni are invited to events only
A few alumni speak or mentor informally, with no record
Alumni roles are recorded and at least three alumni contributed in the last 12 months
Alumni roles are recorded and at least three alumni contributed in the last 12 months, each with a defined role and briefing, and participants rate their contribution

evidence.requirement: Records of alumni contributions in the last 12 months.

questions.text: We know our programme cost per enterprise supported and can show how it is calculated.
anchors: Cost per enterprise has never been calculated
A rough figure comes from total budget divided by participants, with no written method
Cost is calculated for some programmes using direct costs only
Cost per enterprise is calculated for each programme, including shared costs, from the accounts
Cost per enterprise is calculated for each programme from the accounts, including shared costs, tracked over cohorts and compared with results to judge value for money

examples: Programme cost report from the accounting system
evidence.requirement: The calculation sheet and the accounts it draws on.

questions.text: Each year our board or senior leaders approve a budget that shows income and costs by programme.
anchors: There is no annual budget
Budgets exist only inside funder proposals
An organisation wide budget exists but not by programme, or it is not formally approved
An approved annual budget shows income and costs by programme
An approved annual budget shows income and costs by programme, a mid year revision is approved and variances are explained

evidence.requirement: Approved annual budget and the minute that approved it.

questions.text: We share costs such as rent, management and shared staff across programmes using a written method.
anchors: Shared costs are charged to whichever grant has money
The finance person allocates shared costs informally
An allocation rule exists for some costs and is applied inconsistently
A written method is applied to all shared costs and used consistently across programmes
A written method is applied consistently to all shared costs across programmes, is approved by the board or funders and is reviewed by auditors

evidence.requirement: Written cost allocation policy and a sample of allocations in the accounts.

questions.text: We compare actual spending with budget at least monthly and act on large differences.
anchors: No comparison of spending with budget
Compared only when a funder asks
Compared quarterly by the finance person with no leadership discussion
Compared monthly by leaders, with differences above a set limit explained
Compared monthly by leaders, with differences above a set limit explained, corrective actions recorded and checked the following month

evidence.requirement: Budget versus actual reports for the last six months and the minutes that discuss them.

questions.text: Our accounts for the last completed financial year were audited by an independent auditor.
anchors: No audit or independent review in the last two years
The audit is older than two years, or accounts are prepared in house only
An independent review or examination was done, not a full audit
A full audit for the last completed year was signed by a qualified firm more than six months after year end
A full audit for the last completed year was signed within six months, with the management letter answered

evidence.requirement: Signed audit report and management letter for the last completed year.

questions.text: Our accounting system records income and spending by donor fund and programme code.
anchors: Records are kept on paper or in one undifferentiated cashbook
A spreadsheet cashbook is used without project coding
A spreadsheet or software uses project codes but not for every transaction
Accounting software with fund and programme codes is used for every transaction
Accounting software with fund and programme codes is used for every transaction, and donor specific reports are produced without manual rework

examples: Chart of accounts with project codes
evidence.requirement: A system extract or trial balance showing fund and programme codes, and a donor report produced from it.

questions.text: No single person can approve a payment, make it and record it.
anchors: One person approves, pays and records
A second person signs only large payments
Dual approval is in policy but not consistently evidenced
Dual approval is documented, and the person who records differs from the approver and payer for all payments
Dual approval is documented for all payments, recorder, approver and payer differ, approval limits are set by role, and auditors or the board tested them with no exceptions in a sample

evidence.requirement: Payment approval policy and a sample of 10 payments with approval evidence.

questions.text: We reconcile every bank and mobile money account to the cashbook each month.
anchors: Fewer than 3 of the last 12 months, or no reconciliations
3 to 6 of the last 12 months
7 to 9 of the last 12 months
10 to 11 of the last 12 months
All 12 months, each signed by a reviewer

evidence.requirement: Monthly bank and mobile money reconciliations for the last 12 months.

questions.text: We submit donor and financial reports by the due dates set in our agreements.
anchors: Under 50 percent on time, or not tracked
50 to 74 percent on time
75 to 89 percent on time
90 to 99 percent on time
All reports on time in the last 12 months, managed with a reporting calendar

evidence.requirement: Reporting calendar and submission dates for all reports due in the last 12 months.

questions.text: Our leaders receive management accounts every month, within 15 days of month end.
anchors: No management accounts are produced
Accounts are produced only for funders or audit
Accounts are produced quarterly or later than 30 days after month end
Accounts are produced monthly within 30 days and reviewed by the director
Accounts are produced within 15 days of month end, include cash position, budget variance and funder balances, and are reviewed by the director and minuted

evidence.requirement: Management accounts for the last three months with dates issued.

questions.text: We track spending against each donor's budget and eligible cost rules, so ineligible costs are found before the funder finds them.
anchors: No tracking; funder queries often reveal errors
Tracking happens only when a report is written
A spreadsheet tracks spending by donor budget with no eligibility check
Monthly tracking by donor budget line includes a documented eligibility check before payment
Monthly tracking by donor budget line includes a documented eligibility check before payment, and the last two donor audits or reviews questioned no costs
questions.riskTag: Donor funds not tracked against rules

evidence.requirement: Donor budget tracking sheets and the latest funder or auditor findings.

questions.text: Our unrestricted reserves can cover core running costs for at least three months.
anchors: No reserves, or under 1 month of core costs
1 to under 2 months
2 to under 3 months
3 to under 6 months
6 months or more, with a written reserves policy

evidence.requirement: Bank statements and the budget. The verifier divides unrestricted cash by monthly core costs.

questions.text: We update a cash flow forecast for at least the next six months every month.
anchors: No cash flow forecast
A forecast is made once a year for the budget
A forecast exists but covers under 3 months or is updated only quarterly
A forecast covers 6 months and is updated monthly
A 6 month forecast is updated monthly, includes funder payment dates, and has triggered early action on a shortfall

evidence.requirement: The latest forecast and its update history.

questions.text: No single funder provided more than half of our income in the last financial year.
anchors: One funder gave over 80 percent, or income shares are not known
Largest funder gave 61 to 80 percent
Largest funder gave 51 to 60 percent
Largest funder gave 36 to 50 percent
Largest funder gave 35 percent or less

evidence.requirement: Audited or management accounts of income by source for the last financial year.

questions.text: Part of our income is multi-year or core funding that is not tied to a single project.
anchors: No such funding, or the share is not known
Under 10 percent of last year's income
10 to 24 percent
25 to 49 percent
50 percent or more

evidence.requirement: Funder agreements and income schedule showing multi-year or unrestricted income.

questions.text: We earn income from fees, services or success fees.
anchors: No earned income, or the share is not known
Under 5 percent of last year's income
5 to 14 percent
15 to 29 percent
30 percent or more, with prices set from cost data

evidence.requirement: Income schedule showing earned income and the price setting method.

questions.text: We do not depend mainly on unrelated consulting work to keep the organisation running.
anchors: Over 60 percent of income comes from work unrelated to our mission
41 to 60 percent
26 to 40 percent
11 to 25 percent
10 percent or less of income comes from unrelated work

evidence.requirement: Income schedule split between mission work and unrelated work, checked against contracts.

questions.text: We record each introduction we make to investors, lenders or buyers and what came of it.
anchors: Introductions are not recorded
Staff remember introductions but there is no list
A list of introductions exists without outcomes
A register shows date, parties and outcome, updated at least every six months
A register shows date, parties and outcome, is updated at least every six months, and records the value of deals confirmed by the enterprise or financier

evidence.requirement: The introduction register and, for a sample of five, confirmation from the enterprise or financier.

questions.text: Our investor and finance partners are active and suited to the stage and size of our enterprises.
anchors: We have no investor or finance partners
Partners appear mainly at pitch events
Partners exist but several do not fit enterprise size or stage
A partner list shows stage and ticket size fit, and at least half engaged in the last 12 months
A partner list shows stage and ticket size fit, at least half of partners engaged in the last 12 months and at least one made an offer to our enterprises in that period

examples: Offers or term sheets received by enterprises
evidence.requirement: Partner list with stage, ticket size and last engagement date.

questions.text: We check an enterprise's records, numbers and documents with a coach before we introduce it to an investor or lender.
anchors: Introductions are made with no preparation
Enterprises receive pitch coaching only
Some documents are checked with no standard list
A standard readiness checklist is completed with a coach before each introduction
A standard readiness checklist is completed with a coach before each introduction, its results feed into the support plan and investor feedback is collected

evidence.requirement: Completed readiness checklists linked to introductions in the register.

questions.text: We check that the finance offered through our partners has clear, fair terms before we encourage enterprises to take it.
anchors: No review of terms; we promote any offer
Terms are checked informally when enterprises ask
Terms are reviewed for some partners with no written criteria
Written criteria on cost, repayment and collateral are applied to each partner before promotion
Written criteria on cost, repayment and collateral are applied to each partner before promotion, and enterprise complaints about partner terms are tracked and acted on

evidence.requirement: Finance partner screening criteria and completed screens.

questions.text: Our working partnerships with other support organisations, government bodies, banks or buyers are written down, with each partner's role.
anchors: No partnerships beyond informal contacts
Partnerships are mentioned in proposals only
Written MoUs exist for some partners but roles are unclear
Written agreements for main partners state roles, referral rules and a contact person
Written agreements for main partners state roles, referral rules and a contact person, are reviewed yearly, and at least one joint activity or referral per partner is recorded

evidence.requirement: Partnership agreements and a record of joint work in the last 12 months.

questions.text: We keep a list of expected funding opportunities for the next 12 months, with the chance of winning and a person responsible for each.
anchors: No funding pipeline
Opportunities are tracked informally in emails
A list exists without owners or chances
A pipeline shows owner, amount, deadline and chance, reviewed monthly
A pipeline shows owner, amount, deadline and chance, is reviewed monthly and compared with the budget gap, and the win rate is tracked

evidence.requirement: The pipeline file and its latest review.

questions.text: We meet each major funder at least once a year to discuss results and future plans, beyond reporting requirements.
anchors: We contact funders only when reports are due
We contact funders only about problems
We meet some major funders
A yearly review meeting is held with every major funder and recorded
A yearly review meeting is held with every major funder and recorded, and funder feedback led to a change in plan or agreement terms

evidence.requirement: Meeting records with major funders in the last 12 months.

questions.text: When we agree funding, we ask for the real cost of delivery, including a fair share of running costs such as rent and management.
anchors: We accept any budget offered, including none for running costs
We accept low running cost shares because we fear losing funding
We ask for a share on some grants without a rate based on our costs
We apply a written rate based on our costs and report grants that fall short
We apply a written rate based on our costs and report grants that fall short, and agreed rates cover our actual shared costs in most grants
questions.riskTag: Running costs not covered by funders

evidence.requirement: Written running cost policy and the rates agreed in the last three grants.

questions.text: Our board or governing body meets regularly, with minutes and a quorum.
anchors: No board, or no meeting in the last 12 months
One meeting in the last 12 months
Two or three meetings in the last 12 months
Four or more meetings with minutes and a quorum
Four or more meetings, minutes approved at the next meeting, over 75 percent attendance and actions tracked

evidence.requirement: Board minutes and attendance records for the last 12 months.

questions.text: Board members and senior staff sign a conflict of interest declaration each year, kept in a register.
anchors: No conflict of interest rule
A rule exists in the constitution but no declarations are signed
Declarations were signed once and not renewed
Annual signed declarations cover all board members and senior staff, with a register
Annual signed declarations with a register cover all board members and senior staff, and minutes show declared conflicts and the member leaving the decision

evidence.requirement: Conflict of interest policy, signed declarations and register for the current year.

questions.text: The board reviews the director's performance against agreed targets at least once a year.
anchors: No review
Informal feedback only
A review is done but without written targets
An annual written review against agreed targets is minuted
An annual written review against agreed targets is minuted, with development actions and next year targets agreed and followed up

evidence.requirement: Latest director review and the targets it used.

questions.text: We have a written plan for who would lead the organisation if the director left unexpectedly.
anchors: No plan; the organisation would stall
Leaders assume someone will step in but nothing is written
An acting arrangement is named for the director only
A written plan names an acting lead and handover steps for the director and two key roles
A written plan names an acting lead and handover steps for the director and two key roles, deputies are trained, and the plan was tested or updated in the last 12 months

evidence.requirement: The succession or continuity plan and its last update.

questions.text: Our core programme staff stay long enough for the organisation to keep what it has learned.
anchors: Over 40 percent of core staff left in the last 12 months
26 to 40 percent left
16 to 25 percent left
6 to 15 percent left
5 percent or less left

evidence.requirement: Staff list with start and end dates for the last 24 months. The verifier calculates leavers as a share of core staff.

questions.text: When our own expertise is not enough, we bring in outside consultants or partners rather than promise services we cannot deliver.
anchors: We promise services beyond our skills and deliver them poorly
Outside help is used only after problems occur
Outside experts are used sometimes with no rule for when
Skills gaps are listed and outside experts are engaged under written terms
Skills gaps are listed and outside experts are engaged under written terms, expert quality is reviewed and lessons are passed to staff

examples: Quality review of an expert's work
evidence.requirement: Skills gap list and contracts or agreements with outside experts.

questions.text: Every staff member received a documented performance review in the last 12 months.
anchors: No reviews, or under 25 percent of staff reviewed
25 to 49 percent reviewed
50 to 74 percent reviewed
75 to 99 percent reviewed
All staff reviewed, with a development plan for each

evidence.requirement: Performance review records for all current staff.

questions.text: We vet mentors and coaches against written criteria, including references, before they work with entrepreneurs.
anchors: No vetting; anyone willing can mentor
Vetting is by personal recommendation only
Written criteria exist but references and experience are not checked
Written criteria are applied, and references and relevant experience are checked and filed for each mentor
Written criteria are applied, references and relevant experience are checked and filed for each mentor, and mentors have a trial session or probation and periodic re-vetting

evidence.requirement: Mentor selection criteria and the files of five active mentors.

questions.text: Each mentor signs a written agreement on hours, confidentiality, conduct and conflicts of interest before starting.
anchors: No agreement or briefing
Mentors get a verbal briefing only
An agreement exists but few mentors signed it or it lacks conduct or conflict terms
All active mentors signed an agreement covering hours, confidentiality, conduct and conflicts
All active mentors signed an agreement covering hours, confidentiality, conduct and conflicts, renew it yearly and are briefed on the programme and safeguarding rules

evidence.requirement: Signed agreements for all active mentors and the template.

questions.text: We review each mentor's activity and ratings from session logs at least once a year and decide whether to renew, coach or release them.
anchors: No mentor records
Staff recall who is active
Session logs are kept but no individual mentor is reviewed
A yearly review uses logs and ratings, and decisions are recorded
A yearly review uses logs and ratings and records decisions, with weak mentors coached or released and strong mentors recognised

evidence.requirement: Mentor session logs and the latest mentor review record.

questions.text: We have a written safeguarding policy, approved by our board, that covers staff, mentors, volunteers and the entrepreneurs we serve.
anchors: No safeguarding policy
A policy copied from another organisation, not adapted or approved
An approved policy that does not cover mentors or sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment
A board approved policy covers staff, mentors and participants, including sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment
A board approved policy covers staff, mentors and participants, including sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment, adds child safeguarding for under 18s, and was reviewed within 24 months

evidence.requirement: The safeguarding policy, its approval minute and review date.

questions.text: We run a complaints channel that entrepreneurs know about and that accepts confidential reports.
anchors: No complaints channel
Entrepreneurs may speak to staff but there is no defined channel
A channel exists, such as a phone number or box, but entrepreneurs were not told or no confidential option exists
A confidential channel is explained at onboarding, and cases are logged and handled by a named person
A confidential channel is explained at onboarding and cases are logged and handled by a named person, with timely resolution, protection from retaliation and a yearly summary to the board

evidence.requirement: Description of the channel, onboarding material that explains it, and the case log.

questions.text: Staff and mentors complete safeguarding and code of conduct training before they work with entrepreneurs.
anchors: No training, or under 25 percent trained
25 to 59 percent of active staff and mentors trained
60 to 84 percent trained
85 to 99 percent trained, with attendance records
All trained before starting, and refreshed in the last 12 months
questions.riskTag: Staff and mentors not trained on safeguarding

evidence.requirement: Training attendance records for all active staff and mentors.

questions.text: We keep all client enterprise records in one database, with a unique ID for each enterprise.
anchors: Records are scattered across personal files, phones and paper
Several spreadsheets hold duplicate or conflicting entries
One central spreadsheet or tool exists but has no unique ID, or duplicates are found
A central database has unique IDs and shows no duplicates in a sample of 20 records
A central database has unique IDs, shows no duplicates in a sample of 20 records, and has data entry rules and a change history

evidence.requirement: A live demonstration of the database and a check of 20 records for duplicates.

questions.text: Applicant, participant and alumni records are linked in one system, so we can follow each enterprise from application to alumni.
anchors: Applicants, participants and alumni are kept apart or not kept
Participants are recorded but applicants and alumni are not
Applicants and participants are linked but alumni are not followed
All three stages are linked by unique ID, and a sample enterprise can be traced end to end in ten minutes
All three stages are linked by unique ID, a sample enterprise can be traced end to end in ten minutes, and status is updated at least yearly and used for outcome analysis

evidence.requirement: A live trace of three enterprises from application to alumni status.

questions.text: Our client database has complete data on the fields we report on, such as gender, age, location, revenue and jobs.
anchors: Under 40 percent complete, or completeness is not checked
40 to 59 percent complete
60 to 79 percent complete
80 to 94 percent complete
95 percent or more complete, with missing data followed up

examples: Follow up log for missing data
evidence.requirement: A database extract for the last cohort. The verifier calculates the share of key fields filled in.

questions.text: We have a written guide that defines each data field and indicator and how it is collected.
anchors: No definitions; each person records differently
Definitions are known verbally by one person
Definitions exist for some indicators
A written data guide defines all reported fields and collection methods, and staff are trained
A written data guide defines all reported fields and collection methods, staff are trained, a second person checks quality and the guide is updated yearly

evidence.requirement: The data guide or dictionary and training records.

questions.text: We have defined indicators with baseline values for our entrepreneurs, such as revenue, jobs and finance accessed.
anchors: No indicators or baselines
Indicators are listed in proposals but no baselines are collected
Baselines are collected for some indicators or some cohorts
Indicators and baselines are recorded for every participant in the last cohort
Indicators and baselines are recorded for every participant in the last cohort, tied to the theory of change and reviewed yearly

examples: Baseline data for the last cohort
evidence.requirement: Indicator list and baseline data for the last cohort.

questions.text: We follow up enterprises after the programme ends and collect outcome data, not only during the programme.
anchors: No follow up after the programme
Under 25 percent of alumni followed up at 12 months
25 to 49 percent followed up at 12 months
50 to 74 percent followed up at 12 months
75 percent or more followed up at 12 months or later
questions.riskTag: No outcome tracking after the programme

evidence.requirement: Follow up survey or call records for the cohort that ended about 12 months ago.

questions.text: When we report results, we use a comparison group or state how much of the change we can and cannot attribute to our programme.
anchors: All change in participants is claimed as programme impact
Results are reported as before and after with no discussion of other causes
Limits are mentioned in reports but not estimated
A written attribution method, such as a comparison group or other estimate, is used and its limits stated
Participants were compared with waitlisted or rejected applicants for at least one cohort and findings reported

evidence.requirement: Evaluation or results report showing the attribution method.

questions.text: We check a sample of reported results against documents such as sales records, bank statements or payroll, not only entrepreneur statements.
anchors: All results are self reported and unchecked
Staff use judgement but keep no checks
Large claims are occasionally checked, unrecorded
At least 10 percent of reported results are checked against documents each reporting period and recorded
At least 10 percent of reported results are checked against documents each period and recorded, errors are corrected and error rates reported, and a third party reviewed this within 24 months

evidence.requirement: Verification records for the last reporting period.

questions.text: Our leaders use results data to decide which programmes to continue, change or stop.
anchors: Decisions never refer to results data
Results are mentioned in discussion with no records
Results are presented to leaders but decisions are not linked to them
Decision records cite results data for at least one continue, change or stop decision in the last 12 months
Decision records cite results data for at least one continue, change or stop decision in the last 12 months, using rules agreed in advance, and a programme was redesigned or stopped as a result

evidence.requirement: Leadership or board minutes that cite results in decisions.

questions.text: We report disappointing or negative results to our board and funders, not only successes.
anchors: Reports show only successes
Weak results are mentioned only if a funder asks
Weak results are shown to the board but not to funders
Annual reports to board and funders include indicators that missed target, with reasons
Annual reports to board and funders include indicators that missed target with reasons, list lessons and corrective actions, and are shared publicly at least yearly

evidence.requirement: Latest board and funder reports.

questions.text: After each cohort we hold a structured review with staff and entrepreneurs and record the changes we will make.
anchors: No review
An informal staff chat with nothing recorded
A staff only review is recorded
A review with staff and entrepreneur input follows each cohort, with written actions
A review with staff and entrepreneur input follows each cohort with written actions, and the next review checks that earlier actions were completed

evidence.requirement: Review reports for the last two cohorts.

questions.text: Each major programme is reviewed against relevance, effectiveness, efficiency and sustainability at least once per funding cycle.
anchors: No review or evaluation of any programme
Only a funder required final report, with no assessment of effectiveness
An internal review covers outputs only
A written review covers the four criteria for each major programme in the last funding cycle
A written review covers the four criteria for each major programme in the last funding cycle, is carried out or checked by an external evaluator, and has a recorded management response

examples: Programme review using the four criteria
evidence.requirement: Programme review or evaluation reports from the last funding cycle.

questions.text: Our organisation's legal registration and annual filings with the Registrar of Companies are up to date.
anchors: Not registered, or annual returns missing for two or more years
Registered, but annual returns are late or missing for one year
Registered with a current certificate and all annual returns filed
questions.riskTag: Registration or annual returns not current

evidence.requirement: Certificate of incorporation and proof of filing of annual returns, including beneficial ownership information, for the years due.

questions.text: We hold a current licence as a non-profit organisation from the NPO Secretariat and renew it on time.
anchors: No licence, or the licence expired more than three months ago
A provisional licence, or a licence expired within the last three months
A final licence is current and renewals are on schedule

examples: Tax clearance certificate used for renewal
evidence.requirement: NPO licence and renewal filings.

questions.text: Our tax registration and returns with the Ghana Revenue Authority are up to date.
anchors: Not registered for tax, or tax arrears are in dispute
Registered, with returns filed irregularly and arrears outstanding
Registered, with one or more returns late or missing in the last 12 months
All returns filed in the last 12 months with no arrears
All returns filed in the last 12 months with no arrears, a valid tax clearance certificate held and a filing calendar in use

evidence.requirement: Tax registration and filing receipts for the last 12 months.

questions.text: We remit statutory staff deductions, such as SSNIT contributions and PAYE, on time.
anchors: Staff are employed without registration or deductions
Deductions are made but remitted irregularly
Deductions are remitted most months, with some late payments in the last 12 months
All deductions were remitted on time in the last 12 months, with receipts
All deductions were remitted on time in the last 12 months, with receipts, and payroll records are reconciled to remittances each quarter

evidence.requirement: Payroll records and remittance receipts for the last 12 months.

questions.text: Our organisation is registered with the Data Protection Commission and the registration is current.
anchors: Not registered while we hold personal data of entrepreneurs
Registered, but the registration lapsed or its details are out of date
Registration is current and the renewal date is tracked
questions.riskTag: Not registered with the Data Protection Commission

evidence.requirement: Data Protection Commission registration certificate and renewal date.

questions.text: We obtain informed consent from entrepreneurs, explained in plain language, on what personal data we collect, why, and who will see it.
anchors: No notice and no consent record
A verbal explanation only
A notice exists but consent is not recorded for all, or sharing with funders or investors is not mentioned
A written privacy notice and signed consent cover all participants and sharing with funders and investors
A written privacy notice and signed consent cover all participants and sharing with funders and investors, with separate consent for photos and testimonies and a way to withdraw consent

evidence.requirement: Privacy notice and signed consent forms for a sample of 10 participants.

questions.text: We protect personal data with technical and organisational security measures and have a procedure for data breaches.
anchors: No safeguards; data sits on personal phones or shared passwords
Passwords are used but there are no backups or rules
Basic safeguards such as passwords and backup exist but no written rules or breach procedure
Written security rules, role based access, regular backups and a breach procedure are in place
Written security rules, role based access, regular backups and a breach procedure are in place, staff are trained and the measures were tested or reviewed in the last 12 months

evidence.requirement: Data security policy, a demonstration of access controls and the breach procedure.

questions.text: We keep a risk register with owners and review it at least every quarter.
anchors: No risk register
Risks are discussed informally with no list
A risk list exists, has no owners and has not been reviewed in six months
A register with owners and actions is reviewed at least twice a year
A register of programme, financial, safeguarding and reputation risks has owners and actions, is reviewed at least twice a year and is reviewed quarterly by the board

evidence.requirement: Current risk register and review minutes.

questions.text: We check funders, partners and major donors before accepting money or agreements, for example their source of funds and reputation.
anchors: We accept any funding or partnership offered
Informal enquiries are made
Checks are made for some new funders
A written due diligence checklist is applied to every new funder and partner
A written due diligence checklist is applied to every new funder and partner, with periodic re-checks and recorded decisions to decline funding

evidence.requirement: Due diligence checklist and completed checks for the last three new funders or partners.

questions.text: We verify basic facts about an enterprise, such as registration, ownership and key claims, before we endorse it or introduce it to an investor.
anchors: No verification
We rely on what the entrepreneur tells us
Registration only is checked
A checklist verifies registration, ownership and main claims with documents before every introduction
A checklist verifies registration, ownership and main claims with documents before every introduction, checks are recorded and investor feedback on accuracy is tracked
questions.riskTag: Enterprise claims not verified before endorsement

evidence.requirement: Verification checklists linked to introductions in the register.

questions.text: We have a written anti-fraud and anti-corruption policy that staff, mentors and board members have read and signed.
anchors: No policy
A general statement appears in the code of conduct only
A policy exists but is unsigned or not shared
The policy is signed by all staff and board members and sets out reporting steps
The policy sets out reporting steps and is signed by all staff, board members, mentors and partners, with an annual refresher and a case log

evidence.requirement: The anti-fraud policy and signed acknowledgements.

questions.text: We buy goods and services using written procurement rules that require quotations above a set amount.
anchors: No rules; staff choose suppliers
An informal rule only
Written rules exist but are applied inconsistently
Written rules set thresholds and minimum quotations, and purchase records show them applied in the last 12 months
Written rules set thresholds and minimum quotations, purchase records show them applied in the last 12 months, an independent person approves and auditors tested a sample

evidence.requirement: Procurement policy and files for the last five purchases above the threshold.

questions.text: Suspected fraud or misuse of funds is recorded, investigated and reported to the board and affected funders.
anchors: No procedure; incidents are hidden or handled privately
Incidents are handled case by case and not recorded
Incidents are reported to the board only
A written procedure applies; incidents are logged, investigated and reported to the board and funders as required
